heading: What reasoning-bank is
content: This is the official research code release for 'ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory' (Ouyang et al., Google, submitted to ICLR 2026). No CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/docs/ directory -- the README is the only top-level documentation. 'Reasoning bank' means a memory mechanism that distills natural-language 'memory items' (insight/strategy summaries) from both successful and failed agent trajectories, stores them in a bank, and retrieves relevant ones at inference time to prime a fresh agent run. It is not a database/vector-store product -- it is an experimental harness for two benchmarks (WebArena web-browsing agents, SWE-bench/mini-swe-agent software-engineering agents) implementing the ReasoningBank idea plus two baselines for comparison (AWM = Agent Workflow Memory, Synapse = raw trajectory storage), plus a 'memory-aware test-time scaling' extension using parallel-trajectory self-contrast.

heading: Repository structure
content: README.md covers setup for WebArena and SWE-Bench, LLM config, and citation. CONTRIBUTING.md and LICENSE (Apache 2.0, Google copyright headers) are standard OSS boilerplate. main.py, pyproject.toml, uv.lock form a stub uv-managed project where main.py is just a placeholder unrelated to the real logic. assets/ holds two diagram images referenced in the README. WebArena/ is the web-browsing agent experiment pipeline (BrowserGym-based): run.py is the single-task runner that loads the memory bank, retrieves top-n memory, and injects it into agent flags; pipeline_memory.py and pipeline_scaling.py are orchestration loops; induce_memory.py and induce_scaling.py handle trajectory-to-memory-item extraction; memory_management.py is the actual retrieval core; agents/legacy/dynamic_prompting.py has the Flags dataclass and Memory class that render the memory block into the agent prompt; utils/clients.py dispatches GPT/Claude-via-Vertex/Gemini clients. SWE-Bench/ is a thin wrapper (run.sh, compute_stats.py) around a vendored mini-swe-agent in third_party/, which has its own parallel memory/ subpackage.

heading: Core data model -- memory items as JSONL
content: There is no schema file, ORM, or database -- memory is plain JSONL on disk. A memory-bank record looks like: {task_id, query, think_list, action_list, status: success-or-fail, memory_items: [markdown blocks], template_id}. Each individual memory item is a small Markdown block with three fields -- Title, Description (when/when-not to use it), and Content (1-3 sentences of actionable insight) -- generated by an LLM call using prompts SUCCESSFUL_SI/FAILED_SI/PARALLEL_SI in WebArena/prompts/memory_instruction.py. At most 3 items are extracted per trajectory (5 for the parallel/self-contrast variant), and the prompts explicitly ask for generalizable, abstract insight rather than embedding literal task strings. Embeddings are cached separately in parallel JSONL files with schema {id: task_id, text: query, embedding: [floats]}.

heading: Retrieval mechanism -- embedding cosine similarity
content: Retrieval is purely embedding-based cosine similarity, with no keyword or tag search. select_memory()/screening() in WebArena/memory_management.py embeds the current task query using either Gemini gemini-embedding-001 (3072-dim, via Vertex AI) or a local Qwen3-Embedding-8B model (mean-pooled, L2-normalized), wraps the query in a domain-tailored instruction template, computes dot product against all cached embeddings, sorts descending, and returns the top-n (capped at 10, default n=1 in practice) matching entries by task_id. Every new query embedding is appended to the cache file as a side effect, so the cache grows across runs. The SWE-Bench side (third_party/src/minisweagent/memory/memory_management.py) is essentially a duplicate implementation of the same function.

heading: Agent/LLM integration points
content: There is no MCP server, no REST API, and no distributed CLI tool -- integration happens purely by direct Python import within each benchmark's runner. On the WebArena side, run.py writes retrieved memory text into a flat .txt file that agents/legacy/dynamic_prompting.py's Memory class (gated by a use_memory flag) renders into a <memory>...</memory> prompt section. On the SWE-Bench side, third_party/src/minisweagent/run/extra/swebench.py calls select_memory then passes selected_memory=... into DefaultAgent.run() (third_party/src/minisweagent/agents/default.py), which appends the memory text plus an instruction to discuss whether to use each memory item onto the system prompt. LLM clients are abstracted per-benchmark and support GPT-3.5/4/4o, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro, and Claude 3.7 Sonnet via Vertex AI.

heading: Skills/extensions/plugin architecture -- none
content: There is nothing resembling Claude Code skills, a plugin registry, or a hook system in this repo. The closest analog is the --memory_mode switch (reasoningbank / awm / synapse / no_memory) that swaps which prompt/extraction strategy is used -- a simple string-dispatched strategy pattern, not a discoverable plugin system. There is also no test suite and no CI configuration; tooling is uv (lockfile, pinned Python version) plus shell scripts that hardcode environment variables. The .gitignore excludes generated artifacts (config_files/, results*/, logs*/, memories_reasoningbank/), confirming these are all runtime-generated rather than checked in.

heading: What's actually reusable from this repo
content: Not the code itself -- it's a research harness, benchmark-specific, with no server or API surface. The genuinely reusable ideas are: (1) the memory-item schema of Title / Description (when to use) / Content (actionable insight), kept short and generalizable rather than literal; (2) learning from failure as well as success -- distilling insight from failed trajectories, not just successful ones, which is a pattern OB1's thoughts table does not currently implement since it just stores captured thoughts without success/fail framing; (3) retrieval by embedding similarity scoped tightly to the current task and capped small (n=1 to 10), a lighter-weight retrieval philosophy than broad semantic search over an entire memory store.
